bolumler.metin: Did you know an octopus has three hearts?

Two of them pump blood to the gills, and the third pumps it to the rest of the body. But here's the twist: that main heart stops beating when the octopus swims. That's why octopuses prefer crawling over swimming.
Their blood isn't red, either. It's blue, because it uses copper instead of iron to carry oxygen. That works better in cold, low-oxygen water.
The brain is even stranger. About two thirds of an octopus's neurons live in its arms. So each arm can touch, taste, and make decisions on its own.
And they're masters of disguise. In seconds, they can turn into rock, sand, or coral, even changing the texture of their skin.
Three hearts, blue blood, and thinking arms. Are octopuses basically aliens? Tell me in the comments!
